newsitem.title: USA: IVAX gets favorable ruling in patent suit.
newsitem.headline: IVAX gets favorable ruling in patent suit.

text.p: IVAX Corp said Tuesday that a Florida court has ruled in its favor in a patent suit involving terfenadine, the generic equivalent of an allergy drug made by Marion Merrell Dow Inc.

IVAX said it was sued by Dow in 1994 after Dow claimed IVAX could not sell terfenadine because of Dow's patent for a terfenadine metabolite. Dow's patent for terfenadine expired that year, but its patent for a terfenadine metabolite does not expire until 1999, IVAX said.
On Tuesday morning, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida granted IVAX's motion asking that the case be resolved in its favor without a trial, said IVAX spokesman Joe Jones.
The court also refused Dow's request for a ruling in its favor, IVAX said.
Terfenadine, used to treat seasonal allergies, is sold by Dow under the Seldane brand name, IVAX said.
